new_candidates.body:
### What happened?

Since the switch to nanobind (Drake 1.58.0), the object that `LcmBuses.Find()` returns to Python crashes as soon as it is used. It is reported as an `LcmInterfaceSystem`, but calling any method on it aborts the process, and passing it as the `lcm` argument to `LcmSubscriberSystem` segfaults when the subscriber subscribes. (`LcmPublisherSystem` happens to survive because its constructor does not touch `lcm`.) The same code works with Drake 1.50.0.

```python
from pydrake.lcm import DrakeLcmParams
from pydrake.systems.framework import DiagramBuilder
from pydrake.systems.lcm import ApplyLcmBusConfig

builder = DiagramBuilder()
lcm_buses = ApplyLcmBusConfig(lcm_buses={"default": DrakeLcmParams()}, builder=builder)
lcm = lcm_buses.Find("example", "default")
print(type(lcm), flush=True)  # <class 'pydrake.systems.lcm.LcmInterfaceSystem'>
print(lcm.get_lcm_url())  # Crashes ("Fatal Python error: Aborted").
```

My guess at the cause: `LcmBuses::Find` returns a `DrakeLcmInterface*`. nanobind looks up the most-derived type with RTTI, finds the registered `LcmInterfaceSystem`, and wraps the pointer as that type. But in Python `LcmInterfaceSystem` is bound with only `LeafSystem<double>` as a base (see `kLcmInterfaceSystemClassWarning` in `lcm_py.cc`), so the `DrakeLcmInterface` subobject pointer is never adjusted to the start of the `LcmInterfaceSystem`. pybind11's polymorphic downcast handled this.

Workaround: get the `LcmInterfaceSystem` from `builder.GetSystems()` (it is named `LcmInterfaceSystem(bus_name=default)`), which comes back through its `System` base, and pass that instead.

Found in the manipulation course's `MakeHardwareStation(..., hardware=True)` path: RussTedrake/manipulation#620.

### Version

1.58.0 (pip wheel)

### What operating system are you using?

macOS 27 (arm64); the same crash hung our Ubuntu 24.04 CI.

### What installation option are you using?

pip install drake

### Relevant log output

```
INFO:drake:LCM bus 'default' created for URL udpm://239.255.76.67:7667?ttl=0
<class 'pydrake.systems.lcm.LcmInterfaceSystem'>
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```
new_candidates.title: pydrake: object returned by LcmBuses.Find() crashes when used (Drake 1.58, nanobind)

new_candidates.body:
Hi, I was training a diffusion policy on the official PegInsertionSide-v1 motion planning demos and noticed the dataset has a lot of repeated episodes. The file has 1000 trajectories but only 688 unique `episode_seed` values. 312 seeds show up twice, and in every one of those pairs the actions are exactly identical, so effectively about 31% of the dataset is duplicated.

The RL demos for the same task don't have this (1000 episodes, 1000 unique seeds), so it seems specific to how the motion planning data was generated.

I think I found the cause. If you split the 1000 episodes into 10 chunks of 100 (which I assume is one chunk per process), each chunk starts at its own seed block but runs past the start of the next one:

| chunk | first seed | last seed |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 | 132 |
| 1 | 100 | 250 |
| 2 | 200 | 348 |
| 3 | 301 | 480 |
| 4 | 400 | 564 |
| 5 | 500 | 641 |
| 6 | 600 | 750 |
| 7 | 700 | 860 |
| 8 | 800 | 962 |
| 9 | 901 | 1060 |

So, for example, seeds 100 to 132 were generated by both process 0 and process 1. Episode 76 and episode 100 are both seed 100.

Looking at `mani_skill/examples/motionplanning/panda/run.py`, the start seeds are assigned as `range(0, num_procs * num_traj, num_traj)`, so each process gets a block of `num_traj` seeds. With `--only-count-success`, a failed attempt just does `seed += 1` and tries again, so any process that hits failures keeps going past the end of its block and into the next process's range. The dataset metadata points to commit 9d5e0e0, and the logic is the same there as on main now.

Quick way to check:

```python
import json, collections
eps = json.load(open("PegInsertionSide-v1/motionplanning/trajectory.json"))["episodes"]
seeds = [e["episode_seed"] for e in eps]
print(len(seeds), len(set(seeds)))  # 1000 688
```

I haven't checked the other tasks' motion planning datasets, but if they were generated the same way with multiple processes they probably have the same issue. A possible fix would be giving each process seeds that can't collide, e.g. stepping by `num_procs` (`proc_id, proc_id + num_procs, ...`), and maybe adding a note on the demos page until the datasets are regenerated.

Thanks for the great library!
new_candidates.title: PegInsertionSide-v1 motionplanning demos contain 312 duplicate trajectories (overlapping seeds across processes)
